def.en: Due to rising energy costs, more and more companies are investing in improving their energy efficiency in order to save costs in the long term.

short.en: designed or carried out in a way that uses as few natural resources such as water, energy or raw materials as possible

def.en: While resource-efficient production processes initially require higher investment, they pay off in the long term as a result of reduced operating costs.

short.en: the processing of waste materials in order to reuse them as new raw materials or products

def.en: While recycling is still voluntary in many countries, the EU prescribes increasingly higher quotas for certain materials according to stricter legislation.

short.en: an economic model in which products and materials are used, repaired and recycled for as long as possible to minimise waste

def.en: The circular economy is gaining importance due to increasing resource scarcity, while the conventional linear model of produce–use–discard is reaching its limits.

short.en: the obligation of companies or individuals to contribute to the welfare of society beyond their own profit

def.en: Social responsibility, according to growing expectations, goes beyond mere donations and encompasses fair working conditions throughout the entire business operation.

short.en: the voluntary commitment of companies to social, environmental and ethical goals that goes beyond legal minimum requirements

def.en: While CSR was often considered a voluntary extra in the past, it is becoming a strategic factor due to changed consumer expectations and tightened regulations.

short.en: a law that obliges companies to comply with and monitor human rights and environmental standards throughout their entire supply chain

def.en: Due to the supply chain due diligence act, affected companies must carefully vet their used suppliers, while significant fines threaten in the event of violations.

short.en: a trading system that guarantees fair prices and better working conditions for producers in developing countries

def.en: While conventional trade structures often come at the expense of disadvantaged producers, fair trade creates fairer conditions in favour of local communities.

short.en: a written set of rules that specifies how employees or companies should behave in certain situations

def.en: Due to increased compliance requirements, the company has introduced a code of conduct, while violations of it entail disciplinary consequences.

short.en: the principles and values according to which a company acts and makes decisions in order to act in a morally responsible way

def.en: Business ethics is gaining importance due to growing societal expectations, while companies without clearly defined values are increasingly coming under public pressure.

short.en: adherence by a company to all legal regulations, internal guidelines and ethical standards

def.en: Due to tightened legal requirements, many companies have set up dedicated compliance departments, while violations result in heavy fines and reputational damage.

short.en: the abuse of a position of power for personal gain, e.g. through bribery or fraud

def.en: Corruption damages the economy in the long term, as fair competitive conditions are undermined due to lack of transparency, while honest companies are disadvantaged.

short.en: the offering or accepting of money or benefits to induce someone to perform a specific, often illegal action

def.en: Bribery is a criminal offence in Germany, and due to tightened anti-corruption laws, substantial penalties threaten companies and individuals.

short.en: the reporting of misconduct, legal violations or unethical behaviour within an organisation by an insider

def.en: While whistleblowing often entailed professional disadvantages in the past, the EU now offers affected persons better legal protection due to new directives.

short.en: a person who draws attention internally or publicly to misconduct, fraud or legal violations in an organisation

def.en: The whistleblower reported the uncovered misconduct anonymously, while the company had to be contacted externally due to a lack of internal reporting channels.

short.en: the principle that all people should have equal rights and opportunities regardless of gender, origin or other characteristics

def.en: While equal treatment of women and men is a stated goal in many companies, practice often shows considerable gaps due to structural barriers.

short.en: the variety of people in an organisation in terms of gender, origin, age, abilities or other characteristics

def.en: Due to proven advantages, many companies invest in diversity, while homogeneously composed teams often develop fewer creative solutions.

short.en: the principle that all people — regardless of their abilities or differences — participate equally in social and professional life

def.en: While integration means adapting people, inclusion demands that structures are designed from the outset so that everyone can participate.

short.en: the design of environments, products and services so that they can be used by all people — regardless of physical or other limitations

def.en: Due to new EU directives, digital products and public buildings must in future meet stricter requirements for accessibility.

short.en: the principle that all people have the same access to education, careers and social participation regardless of origin, gender or social status

def.en: Equal opportunities have not yet been fully achieved despite existing laws, while structural disadvantages in education and employment continue to exist.

short.en: measures and laws intended to prevent people from being disadvantaged on the basis of characteristics such as origin, gender or religion

def.en: Anti-discrimination is more important than ever due to increasing social diversity, while companies are obliged to actively implement corresponding measures.

short.en: a German law that prohibits discrimination on the grounds of race, gender, religion, disability, age or sexual orientation

def.en: Due to the General Equal Treatment Act, employers must avoid discriminatory job advertisements, while those affected have the right to claim damages.

short.en: the obligation of a company not only to pursue economic goals but also to assume social, environmental and ethical responsibility

def.en: Corporate responsibility today encompasses far more than profit maximisation: due to growing demands, companies must also act socially and ecologically.

short.en: a gas in the atmosphere that retains heat and thus contributes to the greenhouse effect and global warming, e.g. CO2 or methane

def.en: While CO2 is the best-known greenhouse gas, methane and nitrous oxide also contribute considerably to global warming due to their higher warming effect.

short.en: the legal obligation of companies to report regularly on their economic, social or ecological activities

def.en: Due to expanded EU transparency rules, the reporting obligation for sustainability will in future also apply to medium-sized companies, while previously only corporations were affected.

short.en: a collective term for changes in the world of work driven by digitalisation, automation and new work models

def.en: The future of work is shaped by growing automation, while due to demographic change a shortage of skilled workers is simultaneously emerging.

short.en: a concept for a changed world of work that prioritises self-determination, flexibility and meaningful activity

def.en: New Work is gaining importance due to growing demands for self-determination and work-life balance, while rigid hierarchies and fixed working hours are increasingly being questioned.

short.en: a flexible, iterative way of working in which teams work in short cycles, respond quickly to changes and continuously improve

def.en: Agile working enables teams to flexibly change course during ongoing projects and to learn quickly and improve results due to regular feedback loops.

short.en: a project management approach that relies on flexibility, collaboration and incremental improvement rather than rigid plans

def.en: Agile methods rely on regular consultation with the customer during the project, due to which adjustments can be made at an early stage.

short.en: an agile framework in which teams work in short cycles (sprints), hold daily brief meetings and manage tasks in a backlog

def.en: Scrum is a widely used agile framework; during the sprint, clearly defined tasks are completed and due to the regular reviews, they are continuously improved.

short.en: an agile method for visualising workflows on a board with columns such as „To Do“, „In Progress“ and „Done“

def.en: Kanban makes ongoing tasks visible to the whole team, while the limited number of simultaneous tasks prevents bottlenecks due to the WIP limit.

short.en: a short, time-limited work cycle in agile methods (usually 1–4 weeks) in which the team achieves a <g>defined</g> goal

def.en: During a sprint, the team concentrates on clearly defined tasks, due to which a deliverable result stands at the end.

short.en: able to plan, prioritise and carry out one’s own work independently without constant external instruction

def.en: Self-organised teams work independently during the sprint and often achieve better results due to their high degree of autonomy than strictly managed groups.

short.en: the ability of an organisation to react quickly and flexibly to changes and to adapt

def.en: Agility is today one of the most sought-after core competencies, while companies must respond more flexibly than ever due to rapidly changed market conditions.

short.en: an organisational structure with few management levels, in which decisions are made decentrally and closer to employees

def.en: Flat hierarchies foster innovation, while decisions can be made faster due to shorter communication channels than in strictly hierarchically structured organisations.

short.en: an ordered ranking of people or levels in an organisation, in which higher levels have decision-making authority over lower ones

def.en: While steep hierarchies create clear responsibilities, they slow down the organisation’s responsiveness due to long decision-making paths.

short.en: the way in which managers interact with employees, communicate and make decisions — shaped by the values and self-image of the organisation

def.en: Leadership culture is changing considerably during the digital transformation: due to growing complexity, managers are required to act more as coaches than as controllers.

short.en: a transition to new values, behaviours or ways of working in an organisation or society

def.en: Cultural change is inevitable during digitalisation, while companies must fundamentally realign their values and structures due to changed market conditions.

short.en: a new idea, method or technology that significantly improves or changes an existing process, product or industry

def.en: Innovation emerges during the interplay of creativity and willingness to take risks, while companies without continuous renewal quickly lose competitiveness due to changed market requirements.

short.en: the ability to develop original ideas and find unusual solutions to problems

def.en: Creativity is a key competency of the future, while routine tasks are increasingly being taken over by machines due to advancing automation.

short.en: a creative method for solving complex problems, in which the needs of users are at the centre

def.en: Design Thinking relies on interdisciplinary teams, while conventional problem-solving often lacks a user-centred approach due to rigid departmental boundaries.

short.en: a radical change that fundamentally replaces or supersedes existing market structures, business models or technologies

def.en: Disruption fundamentally changes entire industries during a short period of time, while established companies often react too late due to sluggish structures.

short.en: a newly founded company with an <g>innovative</g> business model and high growth potential, often in the digital sector

def.en: Startups frequently fail due to insufficient financing, while those with scalable business models and strong investors grow in the long term.

term.en: willingness to change, openness to change

short.en: the readiness to accept new things, leave familiar paths and flexibly adapt to changed conditions

def.en: Willingness to change is a key competency due to accelerated technological change, while employees without this ability are increasingly difficult to place.

short.en: a skill that is particularly in demand in the digital age, e.g. critical thinking, digital literacy or intercultural communication

def.en: Future skills are becoming increasingly important due to rapidly growing complexity in the working world, while purely technical knowledge alone is no longer sufficient.

short.en: the ability to understand and share the feelings and perspectives of other people

def.en: While machines can process data quickly, empathy is a genuinely human ability that remains irreplaceable in dealing with customers and colleagues.

short.en: acting independently and without constant external control or instruction

def.en: While in the past every decision came from a superior, autonomous working is today becoming the norm due to flat hierarchies and agile structures.

short.en: the ability to argue convincingly in negotiations, find compromises and achieve good results

def.en: While technical knowledge can be learned, negotiating skill remains an ability that only truly matures through experience due to its human complexity.

short.en: a prediction about future developments based on data or experience

def.en: While no one knows the exact future, data-based forecasts provide a sound decision-making basis due to extensive analyses.

short.en: to make contact and communicate with each other, often between humans and machines or between users and systems

def.en: While people used to communicate mainly in person, they now interact in entirely new forms due to digital platforms and AI systems.

short.en: to try something out in practice and test its suitability before deploying it widely

def.en: While the theory sounds convincing, every new concept must be tested in practice before proceeding to broad deployment due to positive results.

term.en: to relieve, to take the load off

short.en: to take work away from someone or a system and thereby reduce the load

def.en: While manual labour used to dominate everyday working life, automated systems can relieve employees today and increase productivity due to optimised processes.

term.en: to control, to manage, to steer

short.en: to direct, control or regulate something, e.g. processes, machines or information flow

def.en: While a person can control machines remotely, networked systems enable an entirely new dimension of flexibility in production due to this capability.

short.en: so clear and logical that one immediately understands and can follow the reasoning

def.en: While the statistics look complicated, the final result is clear: due to consistent digitalisation, the company was able to double its turnover.

short.en: the possibility of working from home instead of commuting to the office every day

def.en: Home office has grown considerably due to improved communication technologies, while employers and employees develop hybrid models as a proven compromise.

short.en: a work model that flexibly combines office work and working from home

def.en: Hybrid working enables greater flexibility, while companies must develop individual solutions due to varying employee needs.

short.en: a work model in which people from different companies or professions work together in a shared office or space

def.en: Coworking fosters exchange between creative professionals, while providing a cost-effective alternative to one's own office due to the shared infrastructure.

short.en: the ability to plan and organise one's own working time so that tasks are completed efficiently and on time

def.en: While distractions in the home office increase, good time management becomes more important than ever due to the lack of external structure.

short.en: the balance between professional demands and personal life that ensures long-term health and performance

def.en: Work-life balance is becoming increasingly difficult to achieve due to boundaryless work, while companies actively counter this with flexible models.

short.en: the conscious separation of work and private life in order to protect one’s own health and performance in the long term

def.en: Setting limits is difficult for many home office workers, while the lack of physical separation due to constant availability leads to a blurred transition.

short.en: the process by which new employees are introduced, integrated and prepared for their tasks in a company

def.en: While traditional onboarding took place on-site, digital onboarding requires new formats and tools due to distributed teams.

short.en: the strategy of companies to retain qualified employees in the long term, e.g. through attractive salaries, development opportunities or flexible working hours

def.en: Employee retention has become a strategic goal due to the growing shortage of skilled workers, while companies without targeted retention measures lose valuable talent.

short.en: the responsibility and effort to actively promote the well-being of people in an organisation or community

def.en: While care was previously mainly associated with the social sphere, it now encompasses occupational health programmes as well due to growing psychological burdens.

short.en: connecting various specialist fields or areas of knowledge in order to solve complex problems from multiple perspectives

def.en: Interdisciplinary collaboration often produces more innovative solutions due to different perspectives, while purely specialist teams risk thinking in their own silo.

short.en: the ability to mediate and coordinate between different specialist areas, departments or systems

def.en: Interface competency is particularly in demand due to growing complexity in networked organisations, while specialists with narrow boundaries often cannot help alone.

short.en: the ability to actively build, maintain and use professional contacts for mutual benefit

def.en: Networking competency has become a core competency during digitalisation, due to which well-connected professionals have a clear advantage on the labour market.

short.en: able to use media and digital tools critically and competently and to evaluate their content

def.en: Media-literate employees can purposefully filter relevant sources during work, due to which they make well-founded decisions.

short.en: a precisely defined sequence of steps or rules by which a computer or AI solves a problem

def.en: While humans used to make decisions, learning algorithms now take over many tasks due to massive volumes of data — from product recommendations to credit checks.

short.en: the ability of computer systems to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, e.g. learning, drawing conclusions or understanding language

def.en: Artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing almost all industries during the coming decades, while intensive social debates are emerging due to unresolved ethical questions.

short.en: a subset of artificial intelligence in which systems learn from data and improve without being explicitly programmed

def.en: Machine learning enables systems to continuously improve during operation, due to constantly growing data volumes and optimised models.

short.en: the use of machines, robots or software to perform tasks without or with little human intervention

def.en: Automation creates new opportunities, while at the same time a shift in the required qualifications takes place due to the elimination of repetitive tasks.

short.en: the scientific and technical field concerned with the development, construction and deployment of robots

def.en: While robotics was previously limited to factories, autonomously working robots are now advancing into many areas of life due to falling costs and growing capabilities.

short.en: the networking of everyday objects and machines with the internet to exchange data and automate processes

def.en: The Internet of Things connects billions of connected devices, while both opportunities and security risks emerge due to the enormous volumes of data.

short.en: extremely large and complex volumes of data that can no longer be processed with conventional methods and require specialised analysis technologies

def.en: Big Data enables precise predictions and decisions due to sophisticated analysis tools, while the protection of personal data remains a central societal challenge.

short.en: the right and technical measures to protect personal data from unauthorised access, misuse or loss

def.en: Data protection is more important than ever due to the growing amount of collected personal data, while the GDPR sets binding minimum standards in the EU.

short.en: measures to protect digital systems, networks and data from cyber attacks, malware or unauthorised access

def.en: Cybersecurity is a critical business task due to increasing digitalisation, while successful attacks cause high financial and reputational damage.

short.en: a network of remote servers on which data is stored, managed and processed without the need for local hardware

def.en: The cloud enables flexible working from anywhere, while companies save considerable IT costs and gain scalability due to shared infrastructure.

short.en: a business model in which digital platforms bring together providers and users and act as intermediaries, e.g. Amazon or Airbnb

def.en: Platform economy is fundamentally changing established business models, while a few dominant platforms control entire markets due to digital network effects.

short.en: a digital infrastructure that connects various users and providers and enables interactions

def.en: While individual companies sell products directly, digital platforms create a new economic logic due to their network effects.

short.en: the concept of how a company creates, delivers and economically benefits from value

def.en: While classic business models relied on product sales, digital models are often based on data and subscriptions due to networked platforms.

short.en: designed so that it can be expanded with increasing demand or scope without fundamental changes

def.en: Scalable business models can reduce the cost per unit during growth, due to which digital companies become profitable more quickly than traditional ones.

short.en: a specific area or division in which a company is active and offers products or services

def.en: While corporations are active in many business areas simultaneously, many startups focus on one clearly defined area due to limited resources.

short.en: the totality of all impressions a person experiences when using a product or service, particularly usability and satisfaction

def.en: User experience has become the decisive differentiating feature due to growing digital competition, while poorly designed products are quickly rejected.

term.en: to operate sustainably, sustainable business practices

short.en: to run a business in a way that combines economic success with ecological responsibility and social commitment

def.en: While profit was once the only goal, sustainable business practices today form part of the standard due to changed stakeholder expectations and tightened regulation.

short.en: an announcement made over loudspeakers in a public place

def.en: Nobody in the terminal should miss an important announcement, as it concerns all passengers.

short.en: a building from which trains depart and arrive

def.en: At the train station, everyone knows that one should listen carefully to the announcements so that nobody misses the train.

short.en: a site with terminals and runways from which aircraft take off and land

def.en: At the airport, everyone should have their boarding pass ready so that nobody is held up at the gate.

short.en: when a train, flight or bus departs or arrives later than planned

def.en: In the case of a delay of more than one hour, every passenger has the right to contact someone from customer service.

short.en: another means of transport one must take after a journey to reach the destination

def.en: In the event of delays, someone from the service team is responsible for ensuring that all passengers still make their connection.

short.en: the area at the station where the train stops and passengers board and alight

def.en: At platform 7, every passenger waits patiently so that nobody is injured in the crush when boarding.

short.en: the departure of an aircraft from the airport

def.en: For departure, every passenger must be there at least two hours in advance so that nobody is left behind in the rush.

short.en: the arrival of an aircraft, train or bus at the destination

def.en: After arrival, every traveller should collect their luggage from the belt so that nothing gets lost.

short.en: the entrance at the airport through which one boards the aircraft

def.en: At gate C14, every passenger must show their boarding pass so that nobody boards the aircraft without authorisation.

short.en: suitcases, bags and other items taken on a journey

def.en: For luggage over ten kilograms, someone must check in at the counter, as one cannot stow it in the cabin baggage.

short.en: to officially register at the airport or hotel

def.en: Before anyone passes through security, one must check in online or at the counter.

short.en: to officially leave the hotel and return the key

def.en: When checking out, every guest must hand in their room key so that nobody forgets to return it.

short.en: an advance booking for a room, table or ticket

def.en: Without a confirmed reservation, nobody can be sure of getting a room if someone arrives at short notice.

short.en: to reserve a seat, room or ticket in advance

def.en: Everyone should book flights and hotels in good time so that nobody pays significantly more when searching at short notice.

short.en: a car with a driver that can be hired for journeys in exchange for payment

def.en: At the airport, everyone can find a taxi, but one should clarify the price beforehand so that nothing remains unclear.

short.en: a car hired for a certain period in exchange for a fee

def.en: With a hire car, everyone can travel flexibly without depending on someone with a fixed timetable.

short.en: an explanation of how to get from one place to another

def.en: When someone needs directions, one should explain them clearly and simply so that nobody gets lost.

short.en: no longer knowing the right way and not knowing where one is

def.en: In an unfamiliar city, one can easily get lost if nobody has a map with them.

short.en: the ability to find one's way in an unfamiliar environment

def.en: With poor orientation in an unfamiliar city, someone can ask at the hotel reception, as one always gets help there.

short.en: the time spent in a place, e.g. in a hotel or city

def.en: For a stay of more than five nights, every hotel guest receives something as a welcome gift.

short.en: a place to sleep and stay when travelling, e.g. hotel, hostel or holiday apartment

def.en: On long business trips, every employee must arrange their own accommodation unless someone from the company takes care of it.

short.en: a building with halls and rooms for conferences, meetings and events

def.en: In the conference centre, every participant finds a place as one can book the rooms in advance.

short.en: a larger, formal event at which experts or representatives of an industry come together

def.en: At the conference, every participant can get to know someone from another country.

short.en: the place where an event takes place

def.en: Every guest should be informed about the venue in advance so that nobody goes to the wrong address.

short.en: the registration desk in a hotel or at an event

def.en: At the hotel reception, every guest receives their key and can ask someone for information.

short.en: to officially register for an event or hotel

def.en: Before anyone can enter the conference, one must register at the entrance.

short.en: an organised event with a specific purpose, e.g. a congress, trade fair or company event

def.en: For the event, every participant must be registered in advance so that nobody is admitted without an invitation.

short.en: a list of departure and arrival times of trains, buses or flights

def.en: In the timetable, everyone can find the departure times, but nobody can guarantee that the trains will run on time.

short.en: a document listing all costs of a business trip in order to have them reimbursed

def.en: After the trip, every employee must submit a travel expense report so that nobody is left with their own costs.

short.en: an estimate of the expected costs before a job or project begins

def.en: Before the trip, everyone should obtain a cost estimate so that nobody faces unexpected expenses.

short.en: a company that organises and sells travel, hotels and tickets

def.en: At the travel agency, everyone can book a trip and be advised by someone with experience.

short.en: a document confirming that a reservation has been successfully made

def.en: Without a booking confirmation, nobody can be sure whether the reservation has actually gone through.

short.en: an amount of money that must be paid when a booking is cancelled

def.en: The cancellation fee applies to everyone who cancels after the deadline so that nobody cancels at short notice without consequences.

short.en: a fixed amount reimbursed per day for accommodation or meals on business trips

def.en: The overnight allowance is the same for every employee so that nobody receives significantly more or less.

short.en: a car that a company provides to its employees for business journeys

def.en: With the company car, every authorised employee can travel flexibly to client appointments without depending on anyone.

short.en: a device or app that shows the route to a destination using GPS

def.en: With a navigation system, everyone can find the way even if nobody knows the road.

short.en: a flat-rate amount reimbursed for meal costs on business trips

def.en: Every employee on a business trip automatically receives the daily allowance so that nobody has to spend their own money on meals.

term.en: travel fund, petty cash for travel

short.en: a sum of money given to an employee in advance before a business trip

def.en: From the travel fund, every employee receives some money in advance so that nobody runs into financial difficulties on the road.

short.en: an indication of a possible danger or problem that should be heeded

def.en: The warning about pickpocketing applies to every traveller so that nobody carelessly leaves their luggage unattended.

short.en: while travelling or moving from one place to another

def.en: On the way, everyone should keep an eye on their luggage so that nobody forgets or loses anything.

short.en: an interruption or problem that hinders normal operations

def.en: In the event of a disruption to rail services, every passenger must wait patiently until someone resolves the situation.

short.en: a time delay in a process or delivery

def.en: Due to a delay at the airport, everyone had to wait — nobody was informed in advance.

short.en: a rule or measure that limits or restricts something

def.en: The luggage restriction applies to every passenger so that nobody brings an excessive amount of weight onto the plane.

short.en: at the shortest distance — right nearby

def.en: In an emergency, everyone should use the nearest exit so that nobody has to cover unnecessarily long distances.

short.en: a bus deployed when trains are not running due to disruptions or construction work

def.en: When boarding the replacement bus, every passenger must wait patiently — nobody gets a reserved seat.

short.en: the enclosed area in a building where a staircase is located

def.en: In the event of fire, everyone must use the stairwell as nobody is allowed to use the lift.

short.en: a designated place where everyone must gather in an emergency

def.en: At the assembly point in front of the building, everyone must stand so that nobody is reported missing in an emergency.

q.en: Could you please connect me with Mr. / Ms. …?

a.en: Yes, of course. One moment please, I'll connect you.

q.en: I think I have the wrong extension. I'm looking for Mr. / Ms. …

a.en: No problem. I'll transfer you. Please hold the line.

q.en: Could you pass a message to Ms. …? She is unfortunately not available right now.

a.en: Yes, of course. What would you like me to tell her?

q.en: I'm not quite sure I understood you correctly. Could you please repeat that?

a.en: Of course. I said: … Is that clear now?

q.en: Feel free to contact us again if you need further information.

a.en: Thank you very much, I will do that. Goodbye!

q.en: Can I help you?

a.en: Yes, please. I'm interested <g>in</g> … Can you tell me more about it?

q.en: Are you also from the … sector / industry?

a.en: Yes, exactly. We work in the … sector. And you?

q.en: We have something very special here. It has the advantage that …

a.en: That sounds interesting. Could you explain that in more detail?

q.en: I'd be happy to demonstrate it for you. You're also welcome to try it out.

a.en: Oh, I'd love that! I'm very interested.

q.en: We have had very good experience with this. The material is made of … and has special properties.

a.en: That's impressive. Is it also available in other versions?

q.en: Can I offer you a small refreshment?

a.en: Yes, please. Thank you very much for the offer.

q.en: If you'd like, I can send you some information material. May we also inform you about new products?

a.en: Yes, that would be very kind. Here is my business card.

q.en: Could you please help me with …?

a.en: Of course, I'd be happy to. What exactly can I help you with?

q.en: So, we have the challenge that delivery times keep getting delayed. I see the main problem in the fact that the supplier doesn't inform us reliably.

a.en: Did I understand you correctly: it's mainly about the poor communication with the supplier?

q.en: Exactly. What consequences do you think this would have if we don't solve the problem?

a.en: What could we do in this situation? Do you have a suggestion on how we should proceed?

q.en: I have an idea or a suggestion: we could, for example, plan a second supplier as a backup.

a.en: <g>It</g> would make sense if we tested that in the short term. An alternative would also be to increase stock levels.

q.en: What do you think about implementing both measures at the same time? How do you see it?

a.en: I think that would be too much at once. From my point of view, it speaks in favor of first testing the second supplier.

q.en: But the argument against that is that it costs us time. Would you agree to start both steps in parallel?

a.en: That sounds convincing. I agree with that, because that way we'll find a solution faster.

q.en: Good idea, however we should also consider that management has to agree. I see it differently: we should first prepare a short report.

a.en: Let's note down the following points: report, cost overview and schedule. What can we agree on?

q.en: We prioritize the report first, then the schedule. Who takes on which task? By when?

a.en: As a compromise, we could split the tasks between the two of us. If we deliver by Friday, would that be acceptable for you?

q.en: We could find a middle ground <g>by</g> writing the report together and creating the schedule separately.

a.en: Let's summarize: we will write the report together. So, this is how we'll do it now: I'll take care of the schedule.

q.en: Next steps are: finalize the report, Mr. Schmidt is responsible, deadline: Friday. What exactly do you mean by 'finalize'?

a.en: By that I mean that all the figures <g>have been checked</g> and the document <g>has been sent</g> to management. Thank you, then we agree.

q.en: I find <g>it</g> quite annoying that the delivery arrived late again.

a.en: That is extremely regrettable. I apologize once again for the delay.

q.en: We are very dissatisfied because the <g>delivered</g> goods do not match the order.

a.en: We very much regret that problems have arisen with your order. The reason for this was an internal error in the warehouse.

q.en: We had to determine that several items arrived damaged. That means we cannot use the entire delivery.

a.en: We are very sorry about that too. We have since found out that the damage occurred during transport.

q.en: I assume that you will accommodate us here and solve the problem quickly.

a.en: We understand very well that you want a quick solution. Would you agree to a free replacement product as compensation?

q.en: We can only agree to that if you also reimburse us for the shipping costs. I ask for a quick solution, as we urgently need the goods.

a.en: That is possible. In addition, we offer to reduce the shipping costs and send the replacement delivery by express.

q.en: But then I expect that something like this won't happen again in the future. We assume that you will improve the quality control.

a.en: As compensation, I can also offer you a voucher for your next order. We will do everything to ensure this does not happen again.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I think introducing more home-office days is a good idea.

explanation.en:
„Einerseits“ opens a two-sided argument („Einerseits“ … Andererseits).
„Außerdem“ only adds information, it does not prepare a counterargument.
„Deshalb“ expresses a consequence, not a weighing.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I am of the opinion that flexible working hours increase productivity.

explanation.en:
„Grundsätzlich“ signals a general, fundamental position.
„Einerseits“ expects an „Andererseits“.
„Im Großen und Ganzen“ summarises what has already been said.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I advocate for an extension of parental leave.

explanation.en:
„Ausdrücklich“ emphasises clarity and determination.
„Selbstverständlich“ sounds too self-evident.
„Im Übrigen“ introduces an additional point, not a stance.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} rising energy costs, many households are heavily burdened.

explanation.en:
„Aufgrund + Genitiv“ is most common in formal written German.
„In exam contexts it is preferred over the more colloquial „Wegen“.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I would like to emphasise that further training is an important factor.

explanation.en:
„In diesem Zusammenhang“ refers to the thematic context of what preceded.
„An dieser Stelle“ is spatial/temporal.
„Darüber hinaus“ adds information but does not link to the context.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} current developments, action is required.

explanation.en:
„Angesichts + Genitiv“ means „in view of, considering“.
„Aufgrund“ would be causal.
„Hinsichtlich“ means „regarding X“ — thematic, not evaluative.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} there are also people who find online meetings less effective.

explanation.en:
„Andererseits“ is the classic counterpart to „Einerseits“ introducing the counterargument.
„Außerdem“ would only add.
„Daher / Folglich“ are consequence connectors.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} the advantages, the high financial burden remains a serious problem.

explanation.en:
„Trotz + Genitiv“ expresses concession.
„Wegen / Aufgrund“ are causal.
„Angesichts“ relates to consideration, not contrast.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} it cannot be denied that the reform also carries risks.

explanation.en:
„Dennoch“ introduces a concessive statement.
„Trotzdem“ is more colloquial.
„Allerdings“ restricts but without as strong a contrast.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} the measure is controversial because it may lead to more bureaucracy.

explanation.en:
„Allerdings“ restricts a previous positive statement.
„Hingegen“ directly contrasts two things.
„Allerdings“ sounds more balanced and is more common in exam German.

sentence.en: Some support the measure — {{BLANK}} see it as a restriction.

explanation.en:
„andere hingegen“ is the set paired formula: Manche … andere hingegen.
„andere jedoch“ is grammatically correct but less idiomatic.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} the positive aspects, the disadvantages must not be ignored.

explanation.en:
„Neben + Dativ“ means „in addition to“.
„Trotz“ expresses concession.
„Außer“ means exclusion.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} it is important that companies invest more in sustainability.

explanation.en:
All four express personal opinion. In DTB B2, „Meiner Meinung nach“ and
„Meiner Ansicht nach“ are tested most often. Pay attention to correct word order.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} this argument convinces me because it is based on facts.

explanation.en:
„Persönlich“ emphasises the individual stance.
„Grundsätzlich“ is too general.
„Eigentlich“ would have a concessive nuance.
„Ehrlich gesagt“ is more colloquial.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I consider the proposed solution to be sensible.

explanation.en:
„Insgesamt“ sums up a balanced consideration.
„Im Großen und Ganzen“ is very similar but longer.
„Letztendlich“ focuses on the outcome.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I have come to the conclusion that digital education is forward-looking.

explanation.en:
„Letztendlich“ expresses a final personal judgement.
„Schließlich“ can be temporal.
„Insgesamt“ summarises but does not conclude with a personal verdict.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} your job advertisement of 15 March I hereby apply for the advertised position.

explanation.en:
„Auf + Akkusativ“ is the set phrasing for applications: „Auf Ihre Ausschreibung …“.
„Bezüglich / Hinsichtlich“ are correct but less idiomatic for cover letters.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} your advertisement in the Süddeutsche Zeitung I am writing to you.

explanation.en:
„Bezugnehmend auf“ is the classic opening for formal correspondence.
„In Bezug auf“ is equivalent but less elegant at the start of a letter.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} your letter of 3 March I inform you that we accept your offer.

explanation.en:
„In Antwort auf“ is the formal letter formula for a reply.
„Als Antwort auf“ is more colloquial.
„Betreffend“ introduces a topic, not a reply.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I have carefully reviewed your offer and would now like to respond.

explanation.en:
„Mit großem Interesse“ is a set formula for positive business correspondence.
„Mit Interesse“ is shorter but less emphatic.
„Mit Freude“ sounds too personal.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I refer to our telephone conversation of yesterday.

explanation.en:
„Hiermit“ is a typical opening word in German business letters — it refers to the current act of writing.
„Somit / Damit / Deshalb“ are consequence connectors.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I am happy to be available for any queries.

explanation.en:
„Bei Bedarf“ is the idiomatic letter formula.
„Im Bedarfsfall“ is a slight synonym but rarer. In an exam context „Bei Bedarf“ is the safest choice.

sentence.en: I {{BLANK}} ask you to send me the documents as soon as possible.

explanation.en:
„Ich würde Sie bitten“ is the formal Konjunktiv II for polite requests.
„Ich möchte bitten“ is more colloquial. Konjunktiv II signals politeness.

sentence.en: For any queries I am happy to {{BLANK}} at your disposal.

explanation.en:
„Zur Verfügung stehen“ is the set phrase for readiness to help.
„Zur Verfügung sein“ does not exist.
„Zur Verfügung halten“ means to keep something ready.

sentence.en: We {{BLANK}} present our new offer to you.

explanation.en:
„Wir erlauben uns“ is a standardised polite formula.
„Wir gestatten uns“ is a synonym but rarer in modern business German.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} your positive response we are very pleased.

explanation.en:
„Sich freuen + über + Akkusativ“ is the correct prepositional government.
„Sich freuen + auf + Akkusativ“ would be for future events. Here it refers to the result.

sentence.en: We {{BLANK}} inform you that your order has been received.

explanation.en:
„Hiermit“ refers to the act of writing itself.
„Somit / Folglich“ are logical conclusions.
„Demnach“ means „accordingly“.

sentence.en: We {{BLANK}} you to settle the invoice within 14 days.

explanation.en:
„Wir bitten Sie“ is the standard polite phrasing.
„Ersuchen“ is more formal, common in official language.
„Fordern / Verlangen“ sound too authoritative.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} our previous cooperation we look forward to further collaboration.

explanation.en:
„Aufgrund“ expresses causality.
„Dank“ would also be positive and possible.
„Angesichts“ is more for critical situations.
„Infolge“ emphasises consequences, not motivations.

sentence.en: We are {{BLANK}} to present you with a special offer.

explanation.en:
„In der Lage sein“ is the formal expression for ability.
„Imstande sein“ is a direct synonym but „in der Lage“ is more frequent in written German.

sentence.en: Please let us know {{BLANK}} whether you are interested in our offer.

explanation.en:
„Baldmöglichst“ is the classic expression in business German.
„Zeitnah“ is modern and acceptable.
„Umgehend“ sounds more urgent.

sentence.en: We {{BLANK}} a confirmation from your side.

explanation.en:
„Würden uns freuen“ (Konjunktiv II) is the polite letter formula.
„Freuen uns“ would be Indicative — too direct. Konjunktiv II signals politeness.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} the costs are high, the investment pays off in the long term.

explanation.en:
All four are concessive. „Obwohl“ + subordinate clause is most common.
„Obgleich / Wenngleich“ are archaic. In DTB B2 „Obwohl“ is the safest choice.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} all criticism, the project proved to be a success.

explanation.en:
„Trotz + Genitiv“ expresses concession: despite the criticism being present.
„Wegen / Aufgrund“ are causal.
„Angesichts“ is for confrontation, less for a positive result.

sentence.en: I understand your concerns, {{BLANK}} I would still like to advocate for my position.

explanation.en:
„Jedoch“ introduces the contrasting clause without being as strong as „Dennoch“.
„Trotzdem“ is more colloquial.
„Allerdings“ restricts the previous statement.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I understand the criticism, I do not share it entirely.

explanation.en: „Auch wenn“ + Indicative is correct here — one concedes understanding the criticism but does not share it. In exam contexts check whether Konjunktiv or Indicative follows.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} the previous year, turnover has doubled.

explanation.en:
„Im Vergleich zu“ is the most neutral comparative expression.
„Im Gegensatz zu“ emphasises the contrast more.
„Gegenüber“ is shorter and also correct.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} the old method, the new one is significantly more efficient.

explanation.en:
„Im Gegensatz zu“ emphasises the contradiction/contrast.
„Im Vergleich zu“ is more neutral.
„Statt“ means replacement, not contrast.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} it can be said that the measure was successful.

explanation.en:
„Zusammenfassend“ introduces a conclusion.
„Abschließend“ relates to the close of a speech.
„Insgesamt“ is a summary word but not a typical sentence opener.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} we can note that demand has increased.

explanation.en:
„Abschließend“ signals the last point in an argument.
„Zusammenfassend“ summarises several points.
„Daher / Folglich“ express causal consequence.

sentence.en: The noise level is too high, {{BLANK}} we should take action.

explanation.en: All five adverbs express a consequence. „Daher“ differs stylistically, as it sounds more formal and elegant in standard written German than the more colloquial „deshalb“ or „deswegen“.

sentence.en: The project has failed, {{BLANK}} we must seek new approaches.

explanation.en:
„Folglich“ emphasises the logical conclusion.
„Infolgedessen“ is correct but more formal and longer.
„Daher“ is a direct synonym
both are suitable for the exam.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} rising demand the company has expanded its production.

explanation.en:
„Infolge + Genitiv“ expresses direct consequential causality.
„Aufgrund“ is similar but more general.
„Dank“ has a positive connotation.
„Angesichts“ is for confrontation.

sentence.en: The survey shows that it is {{BLANK}} to drive digitalisation forward.

explanation.en: „Dringend erforderlich“ is the standardised expression in business German for necessary measures. The other variants are stylistically less precise.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} your job advertisement of 1 April I apply for the position.

explanation.en:
„Bezugnehmend auf“ is the classic formal opening for job applications.
„Auf“ is shorter and also idiomatic. Both are accepted in exam contexts.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} it must be admitted that the old solutions have limitations.

explanation.en:
„Auch wenn“ expresses concessive hypotheses.
„Obwohl“ does not require Konjunktiv.
„Selbst wenn“ is more emphatic.
„Trotzdem“ is a sentence adverb, not a subjunctor.

sentence.en: We {{BLANK}} your reply by 30 June.

explanation.en:
„Entgegensehen“ (+ Dative) is the set formula: „Wir sehen Ihrer Antwort entgegen.“
„Erwarten“ would also be grammatical but less formally idiomatic in letter closings.

sentence.en: {{BLANK}} I share the view that more investment is needed.

explanation.en:
„Vollständig teile ich“ means complete agreement.
„Weitgehend“ would be partial agreement.
„Grundsätzlich“ is correct but weaker.

In a German main clause, the conjugated verb is always in position 2. In subordinate clauses (after dass, weil, wenn, etc.), the conjugated verb moves to the end. Example: <g>Weil</g> er krank <g>ist</g>, bleibt er zu Hause (Because he is sick, he stays home).

„Nicht“ usually negates a specific sentence part or stands at the end when negating the whole sentence. „Kein“ negates nouns with an indefinite or no article. Example: Ich habe <g>keine</g> Zeit (I have <g>no</g> time). Er kommt heute <g>nicht</g> (He <g>isnʼt</g> coming today).

Two-part connectors like „entweder...oder“ (<g>either...or</g>), „sowohl...als auch“ (<g>both...and</g>), „weder...noch“ (<g>neither...nor</g>), „nicht nur...sondern auch“ (<g>not only...but also</g>), „zwar...aber“ (<g>indeed...but</g>) link two equal parts of a sentence.

title.en: um zu / ohne zu / (an)statt zu + infinitive

explanation.en: „Um...zu“ expresses purpose, „ohne...zu“ a missing accompanying circumstance, „(an)statt...zu“ an alternative. These only work when the main and subordinate clause share the same subject; otherwise use „damit“, „ohne dass“, „anstatt dass“.

„Wie“ compares equal things (as big as), „als“ compares unequal things with a comparative (bigger than). „Je...desto/umso“ + comparative expresses a proportional increase: Je mehr er übt, desto besser wird er (<g>the more</g> he practices, <g>the better</g> he gets).

„Es“ can be an impersonal pronoun (Es regnet — <g>it</g>ʼs raining), a placeholder for a postponed subject/object (Es freut mich, dass... — Iʼm glad that...), or a correlate before subordinate clauses. It often carries no meaning of its own, just a grammatical function.

„Wer“ introduces a generalizing relative clause without a reference noun (= „whoever...“): Wer zu spät kommt, verpasst den Zug (<g>Whoever</g> comes late misses the train). The main clause often starts with „der/den/dem“ as a correlate.

Fixed combinations of verb + noun that together mean roughly the same as a simple verb, e.g. „in Kraft <g>treten</g>“ (= to take effect), „Anwendung <g>finden</g>“ (= to be applied), „zur Verfügung <g>stehen</g>“ (= to be available). Typical of formal/professional texts.

The passive voice (<g>werden</g> + past participle) shifts the focus to the action rather than the agent. Passive substitutes: „sich lassen + infinitive“ (it can be done), „sein + zu + infinitive“ (it is to be done), or man-constructions.
Indefinite pronouns like „man, jemand, niemand, etwas, nichts, einige, manche, alle, jeder“ refer to unspecified people or quantities. They are declined according to their function in the sentence.

title.en: als ob / als wenn + Konjunktiv II

explanation.en: „Als ob“ / „als wenn“ introduce an unreal comparative clause, the verb is in Konjunktiv II: He acts as if he <g>knew</g> everything. With „als“ alone (without ob/wenn), inversion follows: Er tut, als <g>wüsste</g> er alles.

The stative passive (<g>sein</g> + past participle) describes the result/state after a completed action, not the process itself: Die Tür <g>ist</g> geöffnet (state) vs. Die Tür wird geöffnet (process).

Texts are held together by connectors, pronouns, synonyms and repeated reference to concepts. Words like „dabei, dadurch, dazu, davon, damit“ are important as references back to something mentioned earlier.
„Dadurch, dass“ and „indem“ introduce a modal clause expressing means or manner: He learned the language <g>by</g> reading a lot (Er lernte die Sprache, indem er viel las).

Many nouns, verbs and adjectives require a fixed preposition with a specific case, e.g. „sich interessieren <g>für</g> + Akk.“ (to be interested <g>in</g>), „stolz sein <g>auf</g> + Akk.“ (proud <g>of</g>), „Angst <g>vor</g> + Dat.“ (afraid <g>of</g>). These combinations must be memorized.

In indirect (reported) speech, especially in news reports, Konjunktiv I is often used to signal distance from the statement: He said he was ill (sei instead of ist). When Konjunktiv I is identical to the indicative, Konjunktiv II is used instead.

Verbs can be turned into nouns, often with the endings „-ung, -heit, -keit“ or as a nominalized infinitive: „prüfen“ (to check) → „die <g>Prüfung</g>“ (the exam), „das <g>Prüfen</g>“ (the <g>checking</g>). Typical of a nominal, formal style.
Modal particles like „doch, ja, mal, eben, halt, denn, schon“ donʼt change the factual content but express the speakerʼs attitude, emphasis or mood. They are typical of spoken language.

Participle I (active, -end: „das <g>lachende</g> Kind“ = a child who is laughing) and Participle II (mostly passive/completed: „das <g>gebackene</g> Brot“ = bread that was baked) can be declined like adjectives before a noun.

„Während“ can be a temporal connector („Während er arbeitet, hört er Musik“ — while he works, he listens to music) or a genitive preposition („<g>während</g> des Meetings“ — <g>during</g> the meeting). Other genitive prepositions: „wegen, trotz, aufgrund, innerhalb, außerhalb“.
